> 古之善為道者，非以明民，將以愚之.

This chapter has been read for two thousand years as one phrase: keeping the people ignorant.

The chapter's most important character is not 愚. It is 明.

## 明 is moonlight through a lattice

明: 照也, built on 月 and 囧.

囧 is the window lattice — the grid in the wall.

So the picture inside 明 is not the sun and moon shining by themselves. It is moonlight coming into the room through the lattice and lighting it.

照 is to cast light on. Not to be luminous.

## 明民 is to spotlight people

If 明 is to cast light, then 明民 is: shine a light on people so they can see each other clearly.

And when people can see each other clearly, they can see position — who is higher, who is faster, who has more. Position produces comparison; comparison produces contention.

This is not "enlightenment." It is illumination. And the chapter's question is precisely: does this illumination give people a road, or does it give them a target?

## 愚 is a heart running after a monkey

愚: 戆也, from 心 and 禺. And 禺 is a kind of monkey — 獸之愚者.

A monkey is not stupid. A monkey is restless: it grabs whatever it sees, never stopping.

So 愚 draws a heart that follows the monkey — not a slow mind, an ungoverned one.

## And 愚 was a pronoun

This is the evidence that settles the chapter.

In pre-Qin usage, 愚 is what a person calls himself when speaking to someone above him: 愚以為, 愚竊以為. The character appears this way throughout the 戰國策 and the 史記.

A man saying 愚以為 is not claiming to be stupid. He is saying: what follows has no cleverness in it — no angle, no advantage being worked.

愚 in that period is a posture, not a measure of intelligence.

Which reframes the whole line: 非以明民，將以愚之 is not "don't enlighten them, keep them dull." It is: do not spotlight them into a field of comparison; let them stand without cleverness.

## 民之難治，以其智多

The people are hard to govern because their 智 is abundant.

智 here is not wisdom. It is the calculated, the angled — the intelligence that has learned to work the spotlight.

A population that has been lit will produce 智, because 智 is what a lit surface generates: the move that gets you seen.

## 賊 is to destroy

賊: 敗也. And 《左傳·文公十八年》 gives the hardest definition available: 毀則為賊.

To destroy is 賊. Not to steal, not to take — to ruin.

So 以智治國，國之賊 is not "clever governance is wicked." It is: governance by angle destroys the state. The instrument of 智 is the particular advantage, and a state run on particular advantages is being dismantled from the inside, one advantage at a time.

不以智治國，國之福 — without it, the state is intact.

## 稽式

> 知此兩者亦稽式. 常知稽式，是謂玄德.

稽 is to check against, to examine — the 稽 of 稽考. 式 is the model, the pattern.

So 稽式 is the pattern you check against: knowing both — the destroying way and the preserving way — is itself the standard.

## 玄德深矣，遠矣，與物反矣，然後乃至大順

Dark 德 is deep, is far, and it goes 反 with things — against the direction things are moving.

反 is the same 反 as chapter 25's 反者道之動: the return, the counter-motion.

Then, and only then, 大順 — the great accord.

The order is the chapter's claim: accord is not reached by going along. It is reached by having gone the other way first.

## Why this chapter follows 64

64: don't manufacture; hold the place.
65: don't light the room. A spotlight is the most efficient way to make everyone start manufacturing.

The two are one instruction at different depths: no shaping of the thing, no shaping of the field it stands in.

## A test

Take any system where you have made performance visible — rankings, dashboards, public metrics. Then ask what 智 appeared afterward. The 智 is not a defect in the people. It is what the light grows.
